Scientific judgment — one screening observation is still necessary; the learned λ-versus-p comparison is not yet justified

I inspected CartmanFatass/My-paper-code through the GitHub connector at exact commit 2b8f1ae0ea8c514bd333c45fe11275a2fabfbb81; I did not substitute a newer revision.

My decision is:

Run exactly one evaluation-only, finite-grid headroom-and-heterogeneity screen. Do not train another ONLGR-like learner yet. Proceed to the matched learned λ-versus-p comparison only if the screen passes both gates prospectively.

The prior evidence already gives two useful bounded nulls:

On the supplied B1 numbers, the ONLGR–RAW advantage is not evidence for task-content value, because ONLGR is effectively tied with TIMING-ONLY. Its upper 95% bound against TIMING-ONLY is 0.004876, so a task-content contribution of at least 0.005 direct normalized-return units is already unsupported on those coordinates.

On the supplied B2 numbers, state-dependent RATE-FLEX does not materially beat state-blind RATE-CONST. Its upper 95% bound is 0.003314, likewise below a 0.005 material threshold.

The older direction record points the same way: ROAD beat RAW, but not NEVER, and only barely SHAM; the repository therefore did not retain a direct-utility interpretation of the action semantics.

Those facts sharply reduce the case for another learned comparison. They do not, however, estimate either remaining quantity directly:

whether any competent, task-blind voluntary-action policy has material direct-return headroom over true inaction and an association-severed action shell;

whether the finite-host direct-return optimum actually requires different non-KEEP probabilities at different pre-action physical-time exposures.

B2’s forced-KEEP panel is useful for pairing and reachability, but it was not a prospective headroom test. The registered B2 design instead tests RATE-FLEX against RATE-CONST with paired seed/checkpoint inference and post-action IID evaluation.

Thus the missing observation is real—but it can be obtained without training a new policy.

The smallest defensible discriminator

Use one rollout package with three sequential decisions:

Stage	Question	Passing condition	Failure consequence
Support screen	Are the physical-time strata actually populated and action-capable?	Predeclared support, event-free reachability, and legal-action requirements all pass	Stop: host does not identify the proposed heterogeneity
Gate 1: headroom	Can a simple stratified action-rate policy materially improve direct return over all competent controls?	All three direct-return contrasts clear +0.005	Stop: bounded no-headroom result
Gate 2: heterogeneity	Does a stratified optimum materially beat the best global p, with a stable ≥0.10 probability difference compatible with increasing exposure?	Value and shape requirements both pass	Only then run learned global λ versus learned global p

The same fixed evaluation bank can support both gates. Gate 2 remains locked unless Gate 1 passes; it is not a second fishing expedition.

the current legal mask;

one shared, frozen conditional REFRESH/REBIND mark rule.

The second item is an important anti-artifact diagnostic: if the stratified ceiling beats the learned RATE-CONST but not the finite-grid global-λ ceiling, the apparent gain is evidence of finite-budget optimization failure, not physical-time headroom.

Preventing privileged outcome access

Before any new candidate returns are examined, partition the IID evaluation coordinates by a fixed seed hash into:

a discovery bank, used to select the grid vector, calibrate the shell, and freeze the mark rule;

an independent confirmation bank, used for every primary contrast.

All 16 recovered seed/checkpoint units should appear in both banks. The unit count therefore remains 16; evaluation episodes and callback boundaries are nested measurements, not extra inferential units.

No checkpoint, stratum, grid point, seed exclusion, mark split, or normalization may be changed after confirmation outcomes are visible. If the selected optimum is on an outer grid point in a consequential bin, report OPTIMUM_UNBOUNDED_BY_GRID; do not expand the grid after seeing the result.

This is cleaner than treating an in-sample maximum over 125 vectors as though it were a learned policy result.

Because the finite-grid candidate is not itself a learned arm, also report the five-point global-λ grid ceiling. A candidate advantage that exists only against the trained checkpoint is a training-budget finding.

2. Genuine no-voluntary-action policy

This arm should:

execute every callback;

compute the legal mask;

perform the same accounting and registered dummy work;

permit exogenous or mandatory host transitions;

always choose KEEP when the decision is voluntary.

It is not “no callbacks” or “freeze the simulator.” It is true voluntary inaction inside the same host shell.

The repository host defines direct reward as service minus action cost and records those components separately. It also instantiates the 4-, 16-, and 32-tick intervals, the 12-tick lease, capped eligible exposure, plan age, downtime, event-free status, and voluntary-event diagnostics.

3. Informative matched action shell

The useful shell is not an effector-null action that pays a cost for accomplishing nothing. Such a SHAM is predisposed to lose and does not isolate the proposed informative association.

Instead use a marginal-rate-matched state-blind action shell:

It invokes the same policy and action machinery at every boundary.

It receives the same current legal mask.

It uses the same event and mark random uniforms.

It performs real legal REFRESH/REBIND actions with the real state consequences and real costs.

It uses the same frozen conditional mark rule.

Its event probability is independent of exposure, tenure, task, and agent identity.

This shell asks the scientifically relevant question:

Does associating action probability with the proposed physical-time variable add value beyond performing approximately the same amount and mix of real action?

It can preserve current-boundary calls, masking, accounting, and expected activity. It cannot preserve future legal masks or future action availability exactly once the policies take different actions. REFRESH and REBIND alter lease and state, so future divergence is part of the total policy consequence. Any claim that a shell exactly matches future availability while taking different actions is internally inconsistent.

Dummy compute is scientifically relevant only if computation affects simulated physical time, reward, or resource use. Otherwise it is an engineering-parity check, not an explanation of direct return.

Tenure should be a sensitivity analysis only. It must not rescue a failed exposure gate. Promoting whichever clock looks better after outcomes would convert the screen into clock selection.

No post hoc quantile bins

Use the existing forced-KEEP panel, or a fresh outcome-blind forced-KEEP support bank on the same coordinates, to determine whether the fixed bins are reachable. Do not replace failed bins with reward-informed quantiles.

A deterministic two-bin fallback could be separately registered, but it should not count as passage of the proposed three-stratum gate. Insufficient support is itself an answer: this host cannot distinguish the requested heterogeneity.

Why strata do not identify a local causal action effect

Eligible exposure, tenure, lease status, failure state, and downtime are all partly consequences of earlier actions. Consequently, a regression such as

R∼action×observed exposure bin

over naturally occupied boundaries would condition on post-treatment state.

The valid estimand here is instead:

The total direct return of a policy assigned at the episode root that maps pre-action exposure bins to fixed event probabilities.

The candidate and controls are randomized or fixed at the policy level. Exposure is an online policy input, not a subgroup in which boundary actions are retrospectively compared.

Event-free reachability helps establish that the high-exposure states exist without prior voluntary interventions, but it does not turn exposure into an exogenous treatment modifier.

The post-action IID ordering is nevertheless important: the next interval is drawn after the current action, so a current policy cannot be credited with predicting the next callback duration. A positive result would concern response to accumulated pre-action time and state, not future-cadence information. The B2 card and host explicitly make post-action IID coordinates primary and schedule the next IID interval after the current action.

Support and competence requirements

The following are proposed design judgments, not facts already registered in the repository.

For every primary exposure bin, require on the confirmation bank:

legal eligible-boundary occupancy in at least 12 of 16 seed/checkpoint units;

at least 25 legal eligible boundaries per contributing unit;

at least 300 pooled legal eligible boundaries;

no single unit contributing more than 20% of pooled support;

event-free reachability in at least 12 of 16 units and at least 200 pooled event-free legal boundaries.

For the selected candidate require:

at least 100 voluntary non-KEEP events overall;

at least 20 voluntary events per exposure bin;

marginal voluntary activity of at least 0.02 among legal opportunities;

both the candidate and global-p policy to retain usable support in all three bins.

For the shell require, on confirmation:

marginal voluntary-event rate within the larger of 0.01 absolute or 10% relative of the candidate;

conditional REFRESH/REBIND proportions within 0.05 absolute, unless the legal mask makes a mark unavailable;

identical action-cost accounting.

If these rate-matching tolerances fail, the shell contrast does not isolate association from amount of action.

A separate mark-specific interpretation requires adequate counts of both REFRESH and REBIND. Otherwise mark choice remains a shared nuisance mechanism and no separate REBIND-value claim is available.

The repository analysis already uses paired seed/checkpoint differences and sign-flip calculations. The new screen should retain that unit structure.

Gate 1 result map

PASS: all three lower bounds exceed +0.005, and activity/support checks pass.

BOUNDED NO-HEADROOM: at least one required contrast has an upper 95% bound below +0.005.

UNRESOLVED: neither bound clears the threshold.

INVALID: support, pairing, accounting, shell matching, or competence fails.

Only PASS unlocks Gate 2. Under this one-shot investment rule, UNRESOLVED does not justify launching the learned comparison.

Both arms then begin with the same marginal activity and receive optimizer updates in a common q-coordinate. This does not make their per-exposure gradients identical, but it greatly reduces a silent parameter-scale advantage.

The learned comparison must also share:

initialization seed;

minibatches and environment-coordinate streams;

update and gradient-evaluation counts;

conditional mark mechanism;

legal masking;

action costs;

optimizer and checkpoint rule;

physical-horizon normalization.

Do not select each arm’s best checkpoint independently. If multiple checkpoints are declared, use the same fixed checkpoints and report the entire paired curve.

Because policies alter their own future exposure distributions, marginal event rates will generally diverge after initialization. That divergence is part of policy behavior; it is not a reason to recalibrate each arm online.

Non-identifiabilities the screen cannot remove

Even a clean positive result would leave several explanations alive.

Callback cadence versus eligible exposure

With declared interval values of 4, 16, and 32 ticks, exposure strata may largely function as labels for those three callback durations. A result can establish finite-host interval-conditioned value, but not a continuous physical hazard.

The 12-tick lease threshold

The 16- and 32-tick intervals cross the 12-tick lease while the 4-tick interval does not. A pattern such as

p
4
	​

≪p
16
	​

≈p
32
	​


could be a simple lease-expiry threshold rather than evidence for the exponential form.

Downtime, failure, and legality

Long elapsed time may co-occur with failures, downtime, expired leases, or different legal action sets. The candidate can exploit those mixtures even without a uniquely exposure-mediated mechanism.

Endogenous tenure and survivor selection

Large plan age is disproportionately occupied by plans that were previously kept and survived. A tenure-dependent optimum is therefore especially vulnerable to post-treatment selection.

Action-mark value

A positive event-rate result may depend on the shared REFRESH/REBIND mark rule. It does not show that REBIND itself carries value, nor that either action has a context-independent effect.

Future shell divergence

Even a properly matched shell cannot hold future masks, leases, and opportunity counts fixed after different actions. A positive total-value contrast is therefore not a pure instantaneous association effect.

Censoring

Exposure capped at 32 and age capped at 64 merge all larger values. A positive upper-bin result cannot distinguish behavior within or beyond the censored tail.

Two-agent interference

Actions can alter shared plan slots, capacity, or service for the other agent. Agents are not independent replications, and the result is not an individual-agent treatment effect.

Optimization geometry

Even with matched marginal initialization, λ and p have different derivatives across exposure values. A learned advantage that does not appear in the corresponding finite-grid ceilings remains a finite-budget optimization result.

Counterexamples that survive an apparently positive screen

Lease-threshold counterexample: the only useful rule is “act after the lease has expired.” Exposure wins because 16 and 32 exceed 12, not because an opportunity-normalized link is intrinsically appropriate.

Failure-proxy counterexample: long exposure is simply a proxy for a higher probability that service has already degraded. An ordinary failure-state policy with equivalent observable information could match the gain.

Cadence-table counterexample: the finite optimum is a three-entry lookup table for callback durations. The exponential form happens to interpolate those three points acceptably but has no standing outside them.

Cost-avoidance counterexample: the candidate’s direct-return gain is entirely reduced action expenditure with unchanged service. That supports sparse action, not rebinding or lease value.

Mark-mixture counterexample: the selected exposure policy reaches legal states in which the frozen mark rule chooses more REFRESH and fewer REBIND actions. The value comes from the resulting mark mixture rather than event timing.

Survivor-selection counterexample: high-age states are populated only by unusually successful KEEP histories. A tenure pattern reflects which plans survive, not a clock-mediated change in action value.

Shell-visitation counterexample: the shell is marginal-rate matched on the reference distribution but induces a different future opportunity distribution. Candidate advantage may arise from this trajectory reshaping rather than information use at otherwise comparable roots.

Training-budget counterexample: the learned λ arm reaches the same finite-grid optimum faster than p under the chosen optimizer. That is a bounded optimization result, not evidence that RAW or global p is representationally incapable.

Decisive early stops and scope invalidators

Stop before Gate 1 if the forced-KEEP pairing invariants fail, any primary exposure bin lacks event-free support, or direct return cannot be reconciled exactly as service minus action cost.

Stop after Gate 1 if any required contrast fails the 0.005 lower-bound criterion, if the candidate is effectively inactive, or if its apparent advantage disappears against the finite-grid global-λ ceiling.

Stop after Gate 2 if the global-p policy is materially equivalent, the probability range is below 0.10, the selected shape is nonmonotone, the near-optimal set contains homogeneous policies, or the result relies on an outer grid point.

Invalidate the screen if:

exposure or tenure cut points are changed after seeing returns;

the discovery and confirmation coordinate banks overlap;

future callback interval or RNG state leaks into the current action;

candidate and controls use different mark heads, action costs, masks, normalization, checkpoints, or evaluation coordinates;

the shell merely suppresses effects while retaining costs and is treated as the association control;

boundaries, events, intervals, or the two agents are treated as independent inferential samples;

tenure is substituted after exposure fails;

service is treated as the primary endpoint when direct return fails;

a positive result is described as future-cadence prediction, a literal hazard, causal lease value, generic REBIND value, arbitrary-k generalization, variable-population evidence, UAV evidence, safety evidence, or general PPO superiority.

Final investment conclusion

The retained evidence is already sufficient to discontinue the task-content-flexibility story at a 0.005 direct-return material scale and to regard generic timing/global-rate explanations as the current default. It is not sufficient to close the narrower question of whether any voluntary action has material direct-value headroom and whether the finite-host optimum is physically time-stratified.

Accordingly, the scientifically proportionate next step is a single frozen-policy, finite-grid confirmation screen. It trains no new learner and has a hard result map:

failure of direct headroom: stop;

headroom but homogeneous optimum: stop;

headroom plus nonmonotone heterogeneity: stop;

insufficient support or precision: no-go for the learned comparison;

only material, stable, monotone exposure heterogeneity with direct-return gain over global p: authorize the matched global λ-versus-global-p comparison.

Even that final positive outcome would justify only the comparison on this two-agent host, its 4/16/32 post-action IID coordinates, declared checkpoint and seed set, and fixed optimization budget.
